page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EADSv5 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 307 GB solid-state drive, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, scoring 2702.28, and achieves average scores in Geekbench single-core and text processing evaluations. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by lower scores in multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation tests. Memory bandwidth is average for large block read operations at 39.33 GB/sec, but write operations and small block cached reads fall into the lower performance tier. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also positioned in the lower benchmark bracket.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E8-4ads_v5 offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive multi-threaded processing. The inclusion of a 307 GB local SSD provides fast local scratch space without requiring external storage attachments. This configuration is best suited for memory-intensive applications, small-scale databases, caching layers, and single-threaded data processing tasks where RAM capacity is the primary bottleneck.
